minutes.headline: Cemetery Commission voted to seek a $20,000 fund transfer for gravestone and wall repairs at May town meeting
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Cemetery Commission reviewed draft minutes, fielded a resident's request about winter cemetery access, and worked through its budget lines with the DPW superintendent to reconcile capital, perpetual-care, and sale-of-lots balances. It voted to request a $20,000 transfer from the sale-of-lots fund via the May town warrant for cemetery repair projects, approved spending on a Fish Street Cemetery headstone plaque and stone repairs, heard an update on the North Cemetery back-lot expansion, and discussed reconciling the board's rules and regulations with the town charter and DPW authority, plus staffing needs.

what_happened.line: The Cemetery Commission voted to request a fund transfer from the sale-of-lots account for gravestone and wall repairs, to go on the May town meeting warrant.
The commission approved spending from that same repair fund on a plaque and stonework at Fish Street Cemetery.
The board agreed to draft its own letter supporting a full-time cemetery hire, on top of the superintendent's separate staffing request.
Members agreed to ask the town manager and town accountant to clarify how perpetual-care interest and fund balances are managed.

why_it_matters: The requested transfer becomes a warrant article, so it is town meeting voters, not the commission, who decide whether that money moves from the sale-of-lots fund into cemetery repairs.
A push for an added full-time cemetery position and a rewrite of the board's rules and regulations could change staffing costs and who has authority over cemetery upkeep going forward.
watch_next: The May town meeting warrant vote on the sale-of-lots transfer
The next Cemetery Commission meeting (fourth week of March) for the final minutes and draft rules-and-regulations revisions
